content.title: About
content.content: Ramen bowl with beef is a ready‑to‑cook package that includes ramen noodles, a flavored broth packet and dried beef pieces. The kit also contains dried vegetables and seasoning. Add boiling water, stir and wait 3‑5 minutes for a hot, satisfying meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ramen originated in Japan in the early 20th century, but its roots trace back to Chinese wheat noodles.
Beef in ramen is often marinated in soy sauce, mirin and spices, giving the dish a rich umami flavor.
Dry ramen kits are popular for travel and office lunches because they require no refrigeration.
Japan boasts over 10,000 regional ramen varieties, each with its own broth style.
Ramen broth can be based on pork, chicken, soy sauce, miso or salt.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Beef and noodles provide complete protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Electrolytes
items.content: The broth packet often adds sodium and potassium, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and seasonings deliver B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: A single package offers a defined calorie count, useful for those monitoring intake.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Broth packets can be very salty, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain soy, gluten in the noodles, and food additives that can trigger allergies.

items.title: Quality of beef
items.content: Dried beef pieces may include preservatives; choose brands with minimal additives.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Some ramen varieties use fatty broths, increasing the dish’s calorie density.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour hot (not boiling) water over the contents, stir, and let sit for 3‑5 minutes. Optionally top with fresh vegetables, herbs, a boiled egg or extra soy sauce for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dry components in a cool, dry place, sealed tightly after opening. Use an airtight container. Do not leave the prepared broth at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
